rulings.Case Title: LAURA L. ANGELES VS. A B C AUTO PARTS ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: Plaintiffs' Notice Of Motion And Motion For Preference Pursuant To C.C.P. 36(A), (D)
rulings.Rulings: On Asbestos Law and Motion / Discovery Calendar for Tuesday, September 15, 2026, Department 502, Line 1. Plaintiff's Motion for Order Granting Preference in Setting Case for Trial, and Extending Discovery Cutoff is GRANTED under C.C.P. Section 36(a) and (d). Oppositions filed by Defendants (1) BWDAC, Inc; (2) Sterling Wander LLLP f/k/a Honeywell International Inc. as successor in-interest to Bendix; and (3) Morse Tec LLC, f/k/a BorgWarner Morse TEC LLC, as successor by-merger to Borg-Warner Corporation. Joinder filed by Defendant Pneumo Abex LLC. Reply filed. Plaintiff has submitted the declaration of her treating physician, Dr. Rahul Naik, who opines that there is substantial doubt that Plaintiff will survive beyond two months from the date of his declaration, or until October 11, 2026. (Dr. Naik Decl at 15 [dated August 11, 2026].) Under these circumstances, setting trial within forty-five (45) days of the order granting preference is permissible and consistent with the purpose of Code of Civil Procedure section 36. (Fox v. Superior Court (2018) 21 Cal.App.5th 529, 536 ["For those in Ms. Fox's unfortunate situation, the end may come quickly with little warning; years may pass with gradual, relentless decline before the battle is lost; or, happily, there may be sustained remission after episodic periods of improvement and relapse. Anyone who has ever heard a physician say in these circumstances, "we just can't predict with any certainty," will appreciate that indeterminacy is not only inherent in the situation, but is part of the challenge of dealing with it"].) The Court finds where a party meets the requisite standard for calendar preference under [Code of Civil Procedure section 36] subdivision (a), preference must be granted. No weighing of interests is involved." (Fox, supra, 21 Cal.App.5th at 535; see also, e.g., Miller v. Superior Court (1990) 221 Cal.App.3d 1200, 1204 [statute "grants a mandatory and absolute right to trial preference"]; Swaithes v. Superior Court (1989) 212 Cal.App.3d 1082, 1085 [trial court "has no power to balance the different interests of opposing litigants in applying the provision"]; Koch-Ash v. Superior Court (1986) 180 Cal.App.3d 689, 694 [section 36(a) "must be deemed to be mandatory and absolute" and "no discretion is left to trial courts.] Accordingly, the motion is granted. 1. The trial date is October 26, 2026, at 11:15 a.m. in Department 206. a. Last day pursuant to C.C.P. section 36(f) is January 13, 2026. b. The parties shall follow the California Rules of Court, San Francisco Local Rules, and Local Rule 20. 2. The last day for hearing summary judgment/adjudication motions is October 20,2026. a. Summary judgment/adjudication motions shall be brought on regular notice pursuant to the relevant provisions of the C.C.P., unless the parties stipulate otherwise. b. Before a party files and serves a summary judgment/adjudication motion, it must contact the clerk to make a reservation. c. The Court allows a maximum of four summary judgment/adjudication motions per day to be calendared, unless good cause is found to exceed this number. Contact the clerk to schedule a good cause hearing. 3. Time to respond to written discovery not yet served is shortened to 20 days. a. For written discovery that has already been served, responses are due within 20 days of this hearing or by the date determined by the C.C.P., whichever is earlier. b. Any issue/dispute that requires meet and confer, shall occur in person or via telephone, not by email or letter. 4. Electronic service is considered the equivalent of personal service. 5. The fact discovery cut-off date is October 9, 2026. 6. The expert discovery cut-off date is October 23, 2026. (Part 1 of 2, tentative ruling continues in Part 2 of 2)
